text:
anya: Quick design check: proposing a compactness + rehydration policy for traces to reduce cold storage and speed queries. Different from simple rollups — this uses per-tenant compact shards + a bloom filter index for quick existence checks before rehydrate. Short thread on tradeoffs and chargeback UX.

rachel: Bloom filters sound smart. Main question: false positive rate -> extra rehydrations -> cost. What target FPR are we comfortable with?

zhen: We can aim for 0.1% FPR with a modest size if we shard bloom filters per-day-per-tenant. For large tenants we can allocate more bits. A 0.1% FPR means ~1 extra rehydrate per 1k negative lookups.

oliver: How do we handle multi-tenant keys and privacy? Bloom filters leak presence info.

anya: Good call. We won't expose raw bloom filters. They'll live in a guarded service with ACLs. For external query paths we do a broker call that returns only existence boolean. No raw bitmaps leave the cluster. Also we salt tenant ids and rotate salts monthly.

rachel: Retention tiers you propose? Please add numbers we can plug into cost models.

anya: Proposal draft:
```n14d -> full spans + readable index
60d -> compact shards (per-request compressed JSON); bloom-filter for existence; sampled spans 1% for recent cold debugging
365d -> metrics-only aggregates + route-level histograms
```
This lets us keep full fidelity for two weeks and much cheaper compact storage for 2-12 months.

zhen: Compact shard format: store an ordered list of span events compressed with delta-encoding + op-ids dictionary. We'll retain top-level attrs (tenant, request_id_hash, start_ts, duration_ms, error_flags) for quick faceting. No raw payload.

oliver: Query UX: if someone runs find-span and bloom filter says possible -> we rehydrate; if bloom filter says absent -> return compact-view link. How long is rehydrate expected?

anya: Rehydrate plan: async cold-worker will read compressed shard, decompress + reindex to ephemeral in-memory index, and return full span payload. Expected median RTO for single trace: ~10-20m, p95 2h depending on load. We can add faster paid restores later.

rachel: 10-20 minutes sounds long for oncall. Can we prioritize rehydrates triggered by monitors or incident pages?

zhen: Yes. We'll add priority queue: incident-sourced rehydrates jump ahead and use warm worker pool. That reduces RTO to ~2-10m for those cases.

oliver: Cost attribution: who pays for rehydration egress/compute? We need chargeback rules.

anya: Proposal: small per-rehydrate chargeback to tenant usage (visible on billing). For support-initiated restores we bill as internal cost center until customer consent. We'll also count rehydrate operations against tenant's API quota unless support bypasses.

rachel: Edge cases: what if bloom filters are missing/corrupted? Fallback must be safe.

zhen: Fallback: if bloom filter unavailable -> conservative path: return compact view + enqueue background scan to locate shard (best-effort). We'll also emit alert if BF-service error rate > 0.1%.

anya: Security / PII: compact shards must strip user-identifying attributes before compression, and we must ensure encryption-at-rest for cold buckets. Add KMS-managed keys per-region.

oliver: Operational signals to monitor during pilot?

rachel: Key metrics: bloom_fp_rate, rehydrate_request_rate, rehydrate_latency_p50/p95, percent_queries_served_by_compact_view, cold_storage_gb_delta, support_restore_tickets. Also unexpected-rehydrate-cost per day.

zhen: Pilot scope: 2-week A/B on 10% prod traffic + staging. We'll roll out per-tenant config flags (opt-in) so power users can stay on full retention.

anya: Experiment runbook addenda:
- Kill switch to disable bloom lookup and fall back to existing retention.
- Circuit breaker if rehydrate_cost per hour > $X or if rehydrate latency p95 > 3x baseline.
- Graceful monitor: if bloom_fp_rate spikes, reduce BF precision (more bits) for offending tenant or pause bloom for that tenant.

oliver: What about developer tooling? We should add a "rehydration request" button in the trace UI that shows cost, ETA, and an option to mark as "priority (incident)".

anya: Agreed. I'll sketch the UI copy: "Full trace archived — request full rehydrate (estimated ETA: 10-20m, cost: $0.02). Mark as priority to expedite for incidents."

rachel: Please also include a small API for programmatic rehydration with auth checks. That helps automation.

zhen: Sample BF lookup pseudo-code for broker:
```
exist = bf_service.exists(tenant_hash, request_hash)
if exist:
  enqueue_rehydrate(request_hash, priority=default)
  return {"mode":"rehydrating", "eta":"10-20m"}
else:
  return {"mode":"compact", "link":"/compact/view/<id>"}
```

anya: I'll prepare the design doc and include proto examples, storage cost estimates, and the pilot config. Draft name: infra/compact-archive-rehydrate-374500. I'll add the runbook and billing rules.

backup-bot: Pilot ticket created: infra/compact-archive-rehydrate-374500. Dashboards: obs.bloom.fp_rate, obs.rehydrate.latency, infra.storage.cold_compact_delta. Monitors: bloom.service.errors > 0.1%, rehydrate_cost/hr > threshold.

anya: Thanks all. We'll sync again after 3 days of pilot telemetry.
